newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ trading conditions to be tough through '97 -ANZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ trading conditions to be tough through '97 -ANZ.

text.p: Some New Zealand retailers are likely to face relatively tough trading conditions over the remainder of the year, ANZ Bank said in its latest Retailers Focus.
"Talking to retailers, we believe the weakness in retailing evident during the Christmas period has continued in the first two months of 1997," Chief Economist Paul Stewart said.
Data from Statistics New Zealand showed seasonally-adjusted retail sales fell 0.1 percent in the December quarter, and actual sales were up just 2.5 percent on a year earlier.

Stewart said the slowdown in sales growth reflected the generally weaker economy over the past 18 months. A marked slowing in employment growth had been a major driver of recent trends, largely offsetting the July 1996 tax cuts and recent rate falls, which should otherwise have encouraged stronger sales.
Stewart said total sales growth over the next six months will be "modest at best", and discretionary types of spending were likely to fall.

In addition, rises in the number of retail outlets in recent years meant individual retailers were often struggling to maintain sales as market growth slowed. "Increasingly, we're finding that retailers and suppliers are being forced to cut prices to sustain sales, including some that may have avoided passing on all of the benefits of the higher New Zealand dollar to customers over the past two years."
ANZ said the continued rise in the New Zealand dollar would make trading conditions difficult for many exporters, and subdued trade in the that sector would indirectly constrain retail spending.
It said further modest falls in interest rates could well occur over the coming months provided the inflation outlook remained encouraging, which could provide some support for retail sales.

"On balance, however, given our expectation that economic activity in many of the key export-oriented industries will remain constrained in 1997, operators should plan on the basis of relatively modest retail spending trends over the next six months." -- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
